title: Use AI or better not?
instruction: You are building a class app. When is it a good idea to get help from AI, and when better not?

items.text: Write the first version of the quiz from your design
items.why: You decide what the app should do, and then you test it.

items.text: Explain a piece of code you don’t understand
items.why: AI is good at explaining. Try out the result anyway.

items.text: Paste a table with your classmates’ names and allergies into the prompt
items.why: Other people’s sensitive data doesn’t belong in a prompt.

items.text: Let the app decide who goes on the trip
items.why: Decisions about people are made by people who answer for them.

items.text: Solve an assignment that is meant to teach you loops
items.why: You would miss out on the reason you are doing the assignment.

items.text: Suggest ten quiz questions that you then check
items.why: A draft is fine as long as you check the facts elsewhere.

items.text: Send the app to the class with the sentence “AI tested it”
items.why: You have to test it and answer for the result yourself.

debrief: AI is a great helper for drafts and explanations. Keep decisions about people, sensitive data and the learning you are meant to do yourself.
